newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM'S PARTY DIPS AHEAD OF AUSTERITY PLAN-POLL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM'S PARTY DIPS AHEAD OF AUSTERITY PLAN-POLL.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) fell behind the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) in a survey released on Tuesday, a day ahead of the unveiling of the government's austerity programme.

The survey in early April by private polling agency STEM showed support for the ODS dropped five points from March to 22.1 percent, while the centre-left CSSD lost 1.5 percentage points but remained above ODS with 23.7 percent.

The result is disappointing for the senior ruling party and its leader Klaus, who will announce the cabinet's plan to kick start the economy on Wednesday, where a series of budget cuts and belt-tightening measures are expected.

But the three-party centre-right ruling coalition as a whole picked up one full percentage point to open an eight percentage point lead over the opposition on gains to the junior coalition pro-business Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).

The ODA, which elected President Vaclav Havel's former spokesman Michael Zantovsky as chairman last month, gained 4.8 points in the aftermath of its party congress to 13.6 percent, apparently picking up ground lost by Klaus's ODS.
The ODA surpassed the other junior coalition member, the Christian Democrats, which polled at 12.4 percent in April, up from 11.1 percent last month.
"April changes in preferences were triggered mainly by reshuffle of votes inside the coalition," STEM said in its commentary included with the survey.
The unreformend opposition Communists enjoyed support of 10.7 percent of the population, up from nine percent in March, while the ultra-right Republicans remained unchanged at 5.5 percent.
The next general elections are scheduled for June 2000.
